properties.decision:
Anthony, 2026-09-07: "let's retire it. this decision will stay in the graph, so I suppose if we ever one day have a legitimate need for it, maybe we'll resurrect it."

WHAT IT WAS FOR, WRITTEN DOWN SO A RESURRECTOR DOES NOT HAVE TO RE-DERIVE IT. QualityGate modelled the STAGE GATE — the milestone review, not a test. Its properties: `phase` (P0-P5/PM, reflow2's own lifecycle ladder), `criteria` (a JSON array of pass/fail conditions), `status` (pending/passed/failed/WAIVED) and `evaluated_at`. Its extraction hint gave the examples "DAG is acyclic" and "all Requirements have coverage" and said it was usually authored by the workflow rather than extracted from prose.

`waived` is the tell, and it is the reason this was NOT a duplicate of anything else. A test does not get waived; a review board's gate does. The three neighbours all answer per-item questions — a Verification checks one target against its spec, a ReadinessAssessment records one technology's TRL/MRL rung, GATED_ON says one increment needs one technology at one level. QualityGate was the only type that asked about THE DESIGN AS A WHOLE at a boundary, with arbitrary stated conditions and a dated, waivable judgement.

WHY IT WAS NEVER USED — STRUCTURAL, AND MEASURED 2026-09-07, NOT INFERRED FROM ITS EMPTINESS:
  (1) It participates in NO EDGE TYPE AT ALL. Not one of the 65 declares it at either end. A gate could be created and then attached to nothing — not the project it gates, not the phase it guards, not the findings that cleared it. It was an island in the vocabulary.
  (2) `criteria` is a JSON array inside a string, so nothing could evaluate it.
  (3) Its own hint says the workflow authors it, and no workflow was ever written that does.
  (4) DECISIVE: NOTHING IN THE DESIGN CARRIES A PHASE. All 3,984 nodes checked — zero. The P0-P5 ladder is declared on QualityGate and on Fragment and used by zero instances. A phase gate had nothing to gate.

WHAT ACTUALLY REPLACED IT, AND WHY THAT IS THE REAL ARGUMENT. reflow2 computes those conditions CONTINUOUSLY. The hint's own two examples — "DAG is acyclic", "all Requirements have coverage" — are literally what detect_defects and detect_gaps evaluate on every call. A computed check never goes stale; a stored `passed` does. The gate was not abandoned, it was dissolved into the loop, and a recorded snapshot judgement would now be the weaker of the two.

⭐ THE CONDITION FOR RESURRECTION, STATED SO IT CAN BE CHECKED RATHER THAN RE-ARGUED. This is the mechanism that just paid off on the environment compliance parking, which named its own reversal condition on 2026-08-26 and was lifted on 2026-09-07 when the condition was met. Bring QualityGate back when a project needs A DATED, WAIVABLE JUDGEMENT AT A BOUNDARY THAT SOMEBODY SIGNS AND IS LATER AUDITED AGAINST — the case the continuous computation cannot serve, because the auditable thing is the human's decision at a moment, not the condition's current truth. A formal program with SRR/PDR/CDR reviews is exactly that case. If it returns, it needs what it never had: at least one edge type binding it to what it gates, a phase actually recorded somewhere, and criteria in a form something can read.

🛑 THE MIGRATION COST — AND THIS PARAGRAPH REPLACES A WRONG ONE, DELIBERATELY SAYING SO. The first version of this decision claimed the removal "very likely affects nobody" because reflow2's graph holds zero instances and the type never had a constructor. THAT WAS WRONG, and the correction is `fact:retiring-a-node-type-locks-every-existing-graph-out-until-it-is-migrated`. The binding gate is not import, it is STORE OPEN, and it reads the graph's STAMP rather than its contents. A stamp records the SCHEMA the writing binary had, so EVERY EXISTING REFLOW2 GRAPH NAMES QualityGate AND EVERY ONE REFUSES TO OPEN until migrated — reflow2's own, holding zero instances, was refused outright. The error came from probing the import path, getting a true answer, and drawing the blast radius from the wrong gate.

A RETIREMENT IS THEREFORE TWO EDITS, NOT ONE. Removing the type from `schema/verify.yaml` is half; the other half is adding it to `RETIRED_NODE_TYPES` in `provenance.rs`, whose own comment had said "empty so far; grows the day a node type is retired". Without that entry the guard reads an ordinary graph as one from the FUTURE and tells the operator their reflow2 is BEHIND and to rebuild — the exact opposite of the correct action. With it, the message says "predates a schema change — migrate", which is right.

THE RECIPE WAS RUN END TO END ON THIS PROJECT'S OWN GRAPH before shipping: export with a binary that still knows the type, import into a fresh path with the binary that retired it, compare. 3,989 nodes and 21,555 edges in, the same out, nothing lost, stamp 29 to 28. One trap found by falling into it: the stamp lives in the SIDECAR `<graph-path>.meta.json`, beside the store rather than inside it, so copying a store over an old sidecar reproduces the refusal on an already-migrated graph.
properties.name: RETIRED — QualityGate leaves the schema: the phase gate it modelled was dissolved into the detectors, and the ladder it gated was never recorded
properties.rationale:
The agent's first recommendation was retirement on the grounds that the type is read by nothing and has zero instances. Anthony's question — "what was QualityGate meant to capture?" — showed that argument was about the IMPLEMENTATION and not the CONCEPT, and the concept turned out to be real SE vocabulary with no other home in the schema. The recommendation survived, but for a better reason: not that nobody used it, but that the loop already answers its question continuously and better.

Recording it as a Decision rather than deleting it quietly is the whole point, and it was Anthony's stated reason for being comfortable with the retirement. A schema type removed with no record is indistinguishable from a type that never existed, and the next person to want a phase gate would rebuild it from scratch — including the four structural mistakes that kept this one empty. This node is the thing that makes the retirement reversible.

THE COST WAS UNDERSTATED WHEN THIS WAS FIRST WRITTEN AND THE RULING STILL STANDS, but the two are worth keeping apart. Anthony ruled on the merits of the type; he did not rule on a migration nobody had measured yet. The migration is one export and one import and it was proven on this project's own graph, but it is owed by EVERY consumer rather than by none, and that is a materially different thing to ship. If the cost is judged too high for the benefit, the honest lever is not to hide it — it is to reverse this decision, which the record now supports.

WHAT IS STILL NOT ESTABLISHED: whether any consumer graph anywhere holds a QualityGate INSTANCE. It cannot be checked from this repo. It also no longer changes the upgrade action, since the refusal fires on the stamp regardless.
